articleTitle: Low-Profile Leaky-Wave Antenna with Mechanical Beam Steering Using Sliding Slot Arrays for K-Band Communications
abstract: A low-profile leaky-wave antenna with mechanical beam steering is presented for K-band applications. The antenna comprises two radiating layers: a fixed layer and a movable layer. Four sets of slots with different periodicities are etched at the surface of both layers. Sliding the movable layer in four steps exposes different sets of slots on the fixed layer, shifting the main beam at four angles. The radiating layers are excited using a pillbox feeding network based on two substrate-integrated waveguide horn antennas through a coupling slot. Simulations demonstrate that beam steering is realized by moving the top layer in four 0.6 mm steps. The antenna is designed to operate at 20 GHz with 0.7 GHz bandwidth, a maximum gain of 20 dBi, with 3 dB scan loss and -9 dB side lobe level.

articleTitle: Dielectric Target Imaging With THz Chipless RFID Technology
abstract: Terahertz imaging is a groundbreaking technology that has broadened opportunities in non-destructive testing, medical imaging, security screening, and the arts for analyzing ancient artifacts. This study presents a chipless RFID array specifically designed for THz imaging. The chipless RFID is placed on a phantom containing a rectangular rubber object. A THz waveguide is then directed toward it, scanning 6 points on the phantom. Finally, the target image and its location are reconstructed using the Delay and Sum method.

articleTitle: E-Band Amplifier in Commercial 0.12 µm GaN at Beyond Twice fT
abstract: A three-stage E-band amplifier has been designed in a commercial GaN process with an f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf> of only 35 GHz, less than half the amplifier’s target frequency band of 81-86 GHz. Two FET topologies were investigated: standard outside via (OSV) and a butterfly (BF) layout with double backvias. Measured gain exceeded 12 dB for both topologies and output power exceeded 18 dBm at 2 dB compression.

articleTitle: High Quality-Factor Cascaded Photonic Crystal Cavity for Phase Noise Reduction in Terahertz Local Oscillator Signal
abstract: We propose a low-loss one-dimensional cascaded photonic crystal cavity with high-quality factor integrated into an unclad silicon waveguide. This cascaded cavity is conceptually analyzed by temporal coupled mode theory, and its performance is validated using full-wave simulation. The cavity exhibits a high-quality factor combined with high transmission efficiency, which holds potential to precisely select the desired single-frequency component of a local oscillator signal. The simulated results of the proposed cavity show a quality factor of 9,161 at 275 GHz.

articleTitle: Phase Noise Correlation in Bistatic Ultra Wideband Impulse Radars
abstract: A measurement-based method which improves the detection of small movements using bistatic ultra wideband (UWB) impulse radars is presented. We measure the channel impulse response (CIR) in a room with a large reflecting target. The phase of two range bins in the bistatic CIR are studied closer: One corresponding to a known reference path between transmitter (Tx) and receiver (Rx), and one corresponding to the reflector. By exploiting the phase of the reference bin, the root mean square error (RMSE) of the target’s velocity induced by phase noise (PN) is reduced by up to a factor of 9.5.

articleTitle: Recycling Microwave Hairpin Filters Using Laser Micromachining
abstract: The work demonstrates an approach to recycle previously manufactured filter designs by laser micromachining its resonant structure as a method of reducing manufacturing costs and time. A hairpin filter centred at 6 GHz is tuned to 8.3 GHz whilst maintaining low insertion loss (IL) and sufficient return loss (RL) in the pass-band. The relationship between the shift in centre frequency against the tapping length is investigated to ensure acceptable filter performance at the highest tuned frequency.

articleTitle: Extraction of Trapping Voltage and Rate Over an Extended Bias Range for GaN and GaAs HEMTs
abstract: Electron trapping is significant to the performance of modern GaN and GaAs HEMTs. This paper presents a novel and simple technique for measuring the dynamic and steady-state trap voltages across a wide range of biases. Capture and emission rates of a trap can also be measured. In this way, trapping rates down to tens of nanoseconds can be evaluated. Calculated trapping voltages and rates can then be employed in formulating a simulation model.

articleTitle: THz Electrically Tunable Polarization Converter via Graphene-Integrated Metasurface
abstract: This paper presents an experimentally validated THz metasurface integrating graphene for dynamically tunable polarization conversion. The design incorporates a bilayer gold-graphene structure, enabling electrical tunability without compromising resonant performance. The metasurface reflects a linearly polarized incident wave into a circularly or elliptically polarized wave, depending on the applied bias voltage. Specifically, within a voltage range of 0-12 V, the polarization ellipticity of the reflected wave can be adjusted from -0.94 to -0.5 at 240 GHz, while the polarization angle shifts from -23° to 12° at 236 GHz. With its straightforward configuration, broad modulation depths, and low operating voltages, this device holds significant promise for THz communication and sensing applications.

articleTitle: Investigating Detection Resolution in Multi-Static Passive Radar
abstract: Situational awareness in complex environments, requires the ability to locate targets in accurately in Cartesian space. This study investigates the role of system geometry in determining tracking precision within this space using multi-static passive radar systems. Two array topologies, the Uniform Linear Array (ULA) and Uniform Circular Array (UCA), are evaluated through a grid-based spatial resolution analysis, to assess target localization in both bistatic range and Cartesian space. The impact of direct path interference is considered by applying its inverse effect to each grid cell, enabling a more accurate assessment of detection sensitivity. The findings offer practical insights into optimal receiver placement and interference mitigation strategies, contributing to improving the design and performance of multi-static radar systems.

articleTitle: A Compact Power Divider Using a Defected Microstrip Structure
abstract: Defected microstrip structures (DMS) increase the effective electrical length of a microstrip line. This study leverages the DMS technique to achieve a compact design by reducing the physical length of the quarter-wavelength lines in a conventional Wilkinson power divider (WPD). The proposed DMS achieves a 50% reduction in the physical length compared to conventional quarter-wavelength lines. Hence, the compact power divider achieves a 36% overall size reduction compared to the conventional WPD and has an operational fractional bandwidth of 79%.

articleTitle: Improving the Form Factor in the Slot Based Built-in Solar Cell Integrated Antennas
abstract: Slot based solar cell integrated antennas are popular among different type of solar cell integrated antennas due to their simple structure. However, in the built-in solar cell integrated antennas reducing the area used by slot is a challenge while maintaining the antenna characteristics specially impedance bandwidth. In this paper a study is done on different slot based solar cell integrated antenna and how the slot area was reduced while maintaining antenna characteristics.

articleTitle: Copper Mesh Ground Planes for 3D-Printed Substrates
abstract: A common problem experienced when producing microwave components through additive manufacturing is the adhesion of printed dielectric substrates to a ground plane. This paper proposes a solution for fabrication involving the Filament Deposition Method (FDM) approach to 3D-printing. Directly 3D-printing onto a fine copper mesh sheet simplifies the fabrication process and maintains acceptable propagation characteristics for the resulting grounded slab. For further demonstration, a frequency-scanning periodic leaky-wave antenna has also been produced and tested.

articleTitle: The Comparative Study of Additive Manufacturing Technologies for a Ka-band Orthomode Transducer
abstract: This paper describes a wideband 3D-printed orthomode transducer (OMT) designed for Ka-band satellite communications. The OMT architecture is based on a symmetrical turnstile junction with a rectangular waveguide network. Notably, the symmetrical design provides a natural isolation between orthogonal polarizations, achieving a greater operational bandwidth compared to septum-based designs. The fabrication is completed by 3D printing together with manual in-house conductive painting and electroplating. The measurements align well with simulations, which realizes a 37.5% bandwidth and covers the SATCOM Ka-band from 26.5 to 38 GHz. The average insertion loss is 6 dB. The return loss is larger than 37.5 dB at the two rectangular waveguide ports, between which the average isolation exceeds 37 dB. The employment of 3D printing methods and materials also demonstrates the promising application of additive manufacturing technology.

articleTitle: Evolutionary Paths to Systematically Unlocking the Frequency-Selective Potential of 3D Meta-Atoms
abstract: This paper highlights the benefits of advanced multi-material 3D printing technology in enhancing the electromagnetic performance of metasurfaces. By systematically evolving geometric structures, the proposed bandpass filtering meta-atom outperforms existing designs in key metrics, including bandwidth, out-of-band suppression, in-band insertion loss, and transition band steepness, underscoring the significant potential of 3D unit cells. Through the integration of qualitative approach and semi-analytical design algorithm, the geometric topology is fully optimized without imposing substantial computational demands.

articleTitle: A Millimeter-Wave End-Fire Antenna Array
abstract: This paper presents a millimeter-wave end-fire antenna array design with improved compactness and broad-band performance. The proposed architecture introduces a pair of horizontally symmetric two-terminal open-circuit U-shaped dipoles as an alternative to conventional folded dipoles. A half-wavelength resonator excitation is implemented to overcome the characteristic high input impedance of folded dipoles, resulting in dual reflection zeros that enable broadband operation. The miniaturized planar antenna element array measures 0.43λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> × 0.25λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>. Experimental measurements of a fabricated 1 × 4 array with directors demonstrate excellent performance characteristics, including 10 dB impedance matching over a frequency range of 24-34 GHz and a consistent average gain of 10.1 dBi.

articleTitle: Programmable 2-bit Metamaterial for Beamsteering in Smart AgTech Applications
abstract: A programmable 2-bit metamaterial designed for smart agricultural applications is introduced, featuring a dynamic beam-steering capability at 5.3 GHz to allow precise field coverage for soil moisture assessment and crop health monitoring. The proposed metamaterial utilizes different PIN diode configurations to enable directional signal reception, supporting beam steering across an azimuthal range from -25° to +40°. Leveraging phase modulation and e-field effects on individual unit cells, the system optimizes array spacing to enhance signal adaptability. Integrated with minimal software hardware requirements, this versatile metamaterial efficiently collects data on parameters such as humidity, temperature, moisture, and crop ripeness from distributed sensors, enabling real-time decision-making. In addition, the solution offers improved field coverage and precision resource management, presenting a scalable approach to advancing productivity and sustainability in agtech.

articleTitle: Modelling and Simulation of Synchronisation Errors in Multi-Receiver Passive Radar Systems
abstract: In multi-receiver passive radar systems, coherent detection assumes accurate synchronisation between receivers. However, achieving this in practice is challenging. By creating a virtual radar environment we can investigate the effect of time, frequency offset and drift in different receiver configurations. Using the Generalised Canonical Correlation Analysis (GCCA) detector, a high performance coherent detector, the effect on localization performance is analysed under controlled conditions. The key output of this work demonstrates that synchronization errors significantly affect localization performance, particularly where the detection performance is relying on coherent detection. Understanding the impact of synchronization errors is crucial for improving and developing future multi-receiver passive radar and distributed beamforming systems.

articleTitle: Enhanced Learning in Microwave Medical Imaging using Boundary-Overlap-Size Loss
abstract: Loss functions are essential for optimizing the imaging performance of trained deep learning models. Thus, the design of tailored loss functions defines the effectiveness of deep learning imaging models. A loss function based on the three geometric measures of the local suspected lesion area and the global image quality of the reconstructed image is proposed. The function is used to efficiently train customized U-Net++ for reconstructing human brains’ dielectric profiles using microwave imaging modality. The input data for training is the broadband time-domain signals irradiated within an imaging domain by 16 antennas. The achieved results confirm accuracy of the trained model using the proposed loss function in reconstructing tissues images quality and lesion area identification.

articleTitle: Antenna Array with Memory Metal for CubeSats Applications
abstract: In this paper, we proposed a 4×12 expandable antenna array with memory metal for CubeSats applications. First, an X-band 4×4 circularly polarised (CP) microstrip subarray with excellent radiation performance is developed. By deploying memory metal at the rotating joints of CubeSat, the antenna array can work in two different states. Compared with the folded antenna array, the realised gain of the expanded array can be increased by 4.7 dB. The proposed scheme provides a potential application approach for CubeSat communications.

articleTitle: A UHF Cavity-Backed Slot Antenna Buried in Sand
abstract: Microwave and UHF antennas for sensing and communications face challenges related to impedance mismatch and detuning. Recently, cavity-backed rectangular slot antennas have proven effective for applications involving soil, wood, and human tissue. This paper presents a design methodology aimed at improving the performance of these antennas. A resonant rectangular cavity with a matching resonant slot at 2.23 GHz has a directivity of 5.6 dB and an efficiency of 40% in air. The change in the resonant frequency when the slot is buried in dry sand demonstrates the sensitivity to this material.

articleTitle: A High-Efficiency Wideband Antenna Utilizing Low-Cost Substrate Material
abstract: A high-efficiency wideband antenna operating in the Wi-Fi band centered at 2.4 GHz is proposed. Despite being constructed on the low-cost, high-loss substrate material FR-4, the antenna achieves a notable radiation efficiency of approximately 93.2% and a wide frequency bandwidth spanning from 2.11 to 2.81 GHz which is about 28.5%. These features are achieved by using an air substrate, a capacitive feed and a modified feeding cable. The proposed antenna has been fabricated and experimentally evaluated to validate the design concept.

articleTitle: Enhanced Beam Focusing in Two-Dimensional Leaky-Wave Antennas Through Phase Modulation Metasurface for Satellite Communication Systems
abstract: This paper presents an investigation into the near-field phase distribution of a two-dimensional (2D) leaky-wave (LW) antenna enhanced by a phase modulation metasurface (PMM). A single-layer PMM, operating at 11 GHz, is meticulously designed to match the frequency of the 2D LW antenna. Based on the Huygens principle, the PMM is asymmetrically printed on both sides of a dielectric substrate, effectively addressing phase errors across the antenna aperture. This configuration yields a significant improvement in the near-field phase uniformity, enhancing the antenna’s overall performance. The proposed design achieves a far-field peak directivity of 19 dBi and an aperture efficiency of 55%, demonstrating the potential of phase modulation metasurfaces in optimizing beam focusing for 2D leaky-wave antennas.

articleTitle: Low-Cost X-band Doppler Radar for Nadir Velocity Detection
abstract: The low-cost, low power, small X-band (10.5 GHz) Doppler radar module HB100, was designed and is used commercially for movement detection. As with most radars, radial displacements of targets provide positive or negative Doppler shifts – depending whether they are approaching or receding in the radial direction. However, in many applications the movement tangential to the radial direction is of interest as well. The radar return from a short steel pipe (outer diameter 170 mm) rolling at a constant velocity on a horizontal plane was used to investigate the effect on the radar output as the pipe rolled through the E-plane and H-plane radar beams. Given the finite beamwidths (40 degrees and 80 degrees, respectively), the voltage output signal versus time is symmetrical with respect to the Nadir in both the approaching and receding part of the trajectory of the pipe for uniform displacement perpendicular to the radar beam. With a null recording immediately beneath the radar in both planes, the velocity of the pipe is monotonically related to the time between the two major peaks and troughs. This allows the velocity determination of objects moving through the radar beam tangentially.

articleTitle: Shared-Aperture Patch Antenna for Energy Harvesting and Wireless Communications
abstract: A shared-aperture patch antenna for simultaneous RF energy harvesting and wireless communications is proposed. Diodes are integrated into the antenna to convert RF energy into DC power and the diode-to-antenna matching is done through antenna geometry optimization. As a result, the design requires no additional rectifier circuit and matching network. The communications mode is designed to be orthogonally polarized to the energy harvesting mode to improve the isolation.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Wideband TTD Phase Shifter Based on DGS for Beam Squinting Mitigation
abstract: This paper presents a high-performance reconfigurable wideband true-time-delay (TTD) phase shifter based on a defected ground structure (DGS). Impedance matching is enhanced by incorporating two identical microstrip stubs, which function effectively in both the “ON” and “OFF” states of the PIN diodes. A 6-unit DGS-based reconfigurable TTD phase shifter was designed to operate from 0.5 GHz to 2.5 GHz with an insertion loss below 1 dB. Finally, the proposed phase shifter successfully mitigates beam squinting when connected in series within an antenna array.

articleTitle: 24 GHz GaN HEMT Power Amplifier Utilizing Matching Circuit-Less Design Methodology
abstract: A 24 GHz GaN HEMT power amplifier (PA) suitable for Wireless power transmission (WPT) applications with a power added efficiency of 40% has been demonstrated using a standard foundry process with a gate length of 0.15 µm. A matching circuit-less design approach was applied to the design of this power amplifier. This design method has previously been used to achieve amplifiers with good performance at 2.4 GHz and 5.8 GHz. In this study, we applied this technique to the 24 GHz band and confirmed its usefulness.

articleTitle: Optimization of Power and Stability in Wilkinson Power Combiners With Asymmetric PA
abstract: This study presents the optimization method of output power and stability in asymmetric signals using a Wilkinson Power Combiner (WPC). To optimize performance, this paper proposes a two-step approach: first, adjusting the resistor of the WPC, and second, employing an asymmetric Output matching network (OMN) to ensure that each power amplifier (PA) is matched to its optimum impedance. Using the proposed method, three types of prototypes were fabricated and measured at 0.8 GHz, demonstrating a 2.9 dB improvement in output power compared to the conventional structure and achieving an approximately equal phase margin of 141° at the two PAs output node.

articleTitle: Testing the Warkworth 30m Antenna for Possible Deep Space Network Applications
abstract: The preparation for cost-effective tests to evaluate the suitability of the Warkworth 30 m antenna for DSN applications at X-band and S-band is presented. The tests are scheduled to be performed on the antenna in December 2024.

articleTitle: Thermal Analysis for HEMT Compact Models
abstract: For extracting compact thermal models for HEMTs, a Fourier Heat Equation solver is developed. Computed transients show separate first- and fractional-order responses. A simple resistor-capacitor network is derived to model this and the coupling between gates.

articleTitle: Phase Correcting Convoluted FSS Reflectors to Increase Directivity in Fabry-Perot Cavity Antennas
abstract: This paper investigates a method to improve the aperture phase distribution of a Fabry–Perot cavity antenna (FPCA), using convoluted frequency selective surfaces (FSS) to improve uniformity of electromagnetic (EM) wave phase inside the cavity, thus improving peak directivity. To test the effectiveness of the phase correcting FSS to improve peak directivity, four FPCAs were designed to operate at 2 GHz. The first FPCA is a conventional FPCA with a Perspex partially reflective surface (PRS), no walls, a patch antenna emitter, and a copper base reflector. The second FPCA design is the same as the conventional FPCA with a copper base reflector, however its cavity is fully enclosed with copper walls. The third FPCA also has a copper base reflector and a fully enclosed cavity, but the copper walls are replaced with phase correcting FSS walls. The fourth FPCA replaced the copper base reflector with the same phase correcting FSS used for the walls, but they gradually decrease in size to produce an increasing reflection coefficient phase change on EM rays inside the cavity. This had the effect of countering the phase non-uniformity across a conventional FPCA’s aperture and increased its peak directivity to 20.48 dBi, which is 8.42 dBi greater than the peak directivity of the conventional FPCA.

articleTitle: Investigating Angle Sensitivity of a 1-Bit Unit cell for Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces
abstract: In this paper, an investigation is conducted on the angular sensitivity of a tunable unit cell to the incidence signal. The unit cell uses a p-i-n diode to switch between two reflection states with a phase difference close to 180° over 2.4 GHz to 2.6 GHz frequency range. It is linearly polarized and is stable for oblique incidence of angle up to 45°.

articleTitle: Design Automation for Microwave Branch-line Couplers Using Artificial Neural Networks with Self-Adaptive Differential Evolution Algorithm
abstract: The traditional method for designing branch-line couplers relies on a time-consuming labor-intensive trial-and-error process with multiple EM simulation iterations. This paper introduces a novel framework combining artificial neural networks with a self-adaptive differential evolution algorithm (ANNs-SaDE) for automatic design. The effectiveness of this framework is demonstrated through the design of wideband three-stage couplers.

articleTitle: Chiral Metasurface for Asymmetric Transmission and Polarization Conversion in Nonreciprocal Shielding
abstract: This paper presents a compact chiral metasurface with efficient asymmetric transmission and cross-polarization conversion. The design selectively filters the incoming signals based on their propagation direction and polarization, while blocking the corresponding perpendicular polarization. The design achieves a high asymmetric transmission (AT) factor of 0.954 and a polarization conversion efficiency (PCE) of 99.99% over a bandwidth of 13.7% at 3.65 GHz. Furthermore, the unit cell comprises a compact size of 0.17λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">₀</inf> × 0.17λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">₀</inf> and a thickness of 0.01λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">₀</inf>. Simulation results validate the design suitability for next-generation electromagnetic shielding and sensing applications.

articleTitle: Compact Tunable Phase Shifter using Broadside-Coupled Structure with Wideband Coverage for Next Generation Communications Systems
abstract: A compact tunable phase shifter designed for K/Ka band applications, but covering frequencies from 12 GHz to 31 GHz, is presented. The tunable phase shifter is designed using a two-layer quarter-wavelength broadside-coupled structure. Specifically in K-band, it achieves a tunable phase range of 127° within the frequency band of 19 to 21 GHz, accompanied by a phase imbalance lower than ±1°. In the Ka-band frequency range of 29 to 31 GHz, the phase shifter exhibits a phase imbalance of only ±0.2°, with a tunable phase of 119°. The insertion loss remains below 1.5 dB across the entire operational bandwidth. The results underscore the potential of this tunable phase shifter for applications requiring precise phase control and minimal loss in microwave and millimeter-wave communications.

articleTitle: 3D Printed Quasi-Fresnel Lens with Oblique Incidence for Sub-Terahertz Near-Field Imaging
abstract: In this paper, a 3D printed quasi-Fresnel lens with oblique incidence is proposed for sub-Terahertz (THz) near-field imaging. The proposed lens can focus the spherical wave to a focal point on the other side with an incident angle of 30°. The design process is based on the discrete dielectric lens using a uniform dielectric post as a unit cell (UC), and its period is minimised to generate a nearly continuous surface. Phase distribution is calculated using Fermat's principle. The printed prototype is measured by a THz camera, and a focal spot is generated.

articleTitle: Circular Waveguide Probe Using Broadband Dielectric Lens for Skin Cancer Detection
abstract: A nearfield microwave probe for skin cancer detection is presented. The probe consists of a circular waveguide attached to a tapered multilayer dielectric lens. The probe, which covers the band 15-24 GHz, has a contact tip diameter of 2 mm and a sensing depth of 0.8 mm. The probe is designed to ensure significant variations in its reflection coefficient magnitude when in contact with benign and malignant lesions. Thus, a multilayer lens is attached at the end of the waveguide to focus the field inside the skin and enhance the contrast between different lesions and healthy skin. The simulation results show that the probe can identify Squamous Cell Carcinoma (SCC) and its pre-malignant condition, Actinic Keratosis (AK) through a reflection coefficient magnitude contrast reduction of 16.8% and 13.6%, while Basal Cell Carcinoma (BCC) and Benign Solar Lentigo (BSL)have a reflection coefficient magnitude contrast increment of 13.7 % and 34.5% with respect to the healthy skin response.

articleTitle: Metasurface Based WiFi Tag with High Angular Stability
abstract: This paper proposes a WiFi tag design with high angular stability that is passive and suitable for applications such as indoor localization, environmental sensing, and material identification within the WiFi frequency range, utilizing existing infrastructure. It offers advantages including low maintenance cost, simplicity, and accuracy. The tag integrates a metasurface and a retroreflector, demonstrating high angular stability and detectability at normal incidence. In preliminary experiments, the tag can at least operate effectively at a distance of 550 mm.

articleTitle: Low-Profile Transmissive Metasurface for Generating The Butterfly-Shaped Beam
abstract: A low-profile transmissive metasurface is proposed for generating the butterfly-shaped beam. The metasurface is composed of the single-layer dielectric unit cell with vias. The metal on the upper and lower surfaces of the unit cell is consistent, and the shape of each metal layer is extremely simple, consisting of three rectangular patches. The phase distribution of metasurfaces includes two parts: the focusing phase and the periodic phase. The simulation results show that the proposed metasurface can generate a butterfly-shaped beam with a gain of 19.4 dBi.

articleTitle: Human Instancing and Tracking on Sparse mmWave Radar Data
abstract: The need for non-invasive human movement monitoring in healthcare is growing, and traditional methods often involve wearable or use video monitoring. Wearable technology can cause discomfort, and video monitoring has privacy concerns. Our proposed approach uses a Millimeter-Wave (mmWave) Radar to detect and quantify human movement for health applications. One of the challenges in using mmWave radar for real-time detection is processing the range and velocity data readings. The filtered data is often sparse, which is difficult for human instancing and tracking. Our approach uses a machine learning approach with Similarity Group Proposal Network (SGPN) to detect human instancing and tracking using mmWave radar data. We show we can achieve a 94% accuracy in distinguishing between environmental noise and people, though more work is needed to track individual people.

articleTitle: Rigorous Design Approach for Bandpass Filter With Specified Wide Spurious-Free Upper Stopband
abstract: This paper presents a rigorous approach to design a bandpass filter with a wide spurious-free upper stopband. One of the unique features of the presented design method is that a spurious-free upper stopband range can be determined in advance. The presented design approach requires no coupling tests heavily relying on time-consuming electromagnetic simulations. For illustration, we have designed, fabricated, and measured a 4th-order microstrip Chebyshev filter. The second passband was defined to be at 8f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> (f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> : center frequency of the primary passband) so that the filter has a spurious-free region from f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> to 8f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>.

articleTitle: Mitigation of Radiation Loss in mmWave Rotman Lens Beamformers
abstract: The millimeter wave (mmWave) frequency spectrum, essential for high capacity transmission in Beyond 5G (B5G) and 6<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> Generation (6G) communication systems, requires efficient and precise beamforming solutions. The Rotman Lens (RL), known for its low-cost fabrication, design simplicity, wide bandwidth, and wide-angle scanning capabilities, has been extensively used in beamforming networks. Traditionally, Microstrip Line (MSL) technology is employed to develop RL. However, MSL-based RL suffers from considerable radiation losses in addition to insertion losses due to impedance mismatch. The radiation loss is prominent at mmWave frequencies, which degrades the RL performance. To overcome these challenges, the Substrate Integrated Coaxial Line (SICL) technology offers an improved alternative for RL development, making them highly effective for beamforming and multiplexing operations. This paper discusses the design challenges and performance of SICL-RL, to study enhanced phase accuracy, and wide-angle scanning capabilities for mmWave applications.

articleTitle: Experimental Real-Time Electromagnetic Knee Imaging Using Pattern and Polarization Diversity
abstract: An electromagnetic imaging system for real-time knee injury detection and monitoring is presented. The system features an 8-element MIMO antenna array with pattern and polarization diversity designed to operate over a wide bandwidth (0.8–2.7 GHz). Each MIMO element employs four orthogonal feed lines and a substrate-integrated waveguide cavity for enhanced directivity and unidirectional radiation. A flexible matched layer is used to ensure efficient energy transfer and compatibility with the dynamic knee motion. The MIMO module is fabricated and tested on a realistic knee phantom. A modified delay-and-sum imaging algorithm is used to generate knee images for cases emulating various scenarios, considering early-stage cases and the challenges of dynamic movement. The results demonstrate the capability of the system to accurately detect and localize ligament tears, outperforming conventional linear and dual-polarized systems.

articleTitle: V-band GaAs Power Amplifier Cell
abstract: The development of a compact, 0.1 um GaAs, V-band, power-amplifier cell is reported. The cell is a building block suitable for stacking in order to implement amplifiers with higher power. The cell delivers 23.0 dBm in saturation at 60 GHz with a PAE of 19%. The 3-dB bandwidth is 10 GHz with a peak small-signal gain of 24.8 dB. For the design, a single-finger pHEMT model and foundry model were used and compared.

articleTitle: Wideband Scanning Performance Enhancement of Microstrip Arrays with Low-Profile 3D Loading
abstract: This paper explores a 3D structure to enhance the scanning range of a U-slot microstrip patch array. The solution uses two orthogonal sets of parallel metallic strips along the E-plane and H-plane, improving performance across all three planes (E, H, D) to 70 degrees over 13% of the bandwidth, while keeping the structure height under 0.7λ.

articleTitle: Compact SIW Cavity Backed Dual-Polarized Antenna for Torso Imaging
abstract: A compact, on-body matched substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW) antenna is designed for torso imaging. The antenna has wideband performance and thus the capability of deep power penetration into the human torso. The design includes two central patches to enable dual polarization, left-hand and right-hand circularly polarization, with an auxiliary patch to improve impedance matching. To minimize back and side radiation and enhance electromagnetic penetration into the torso, the SIW technique is utilized by fencing the substrate edges with metalized vias. Simulation results demonstrate that the antenna operates across a frequency range of 0.72 to 1.70 GHz, achieving an 80% fractional bandwidth with more than 10 dB of return loss. The antenna occupies a compact size of 82×82×8 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, equivalent to 0.19×0.19×0.01 ${\lambda _0}^3$, where λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> is the wavelength at the lowest operating frequency. The proposed antenna is a proposed candidate for deep torso imaging.

articleTitle: Microstrip Antenna Miniaturization Using 3-D Printed Substrate
abstract: A miniaturized microstrip patch antenna using a three-dimensional (3-D) printed substrate is presented in this paper. To achieve miniaturization, a triangular prism substrate is proposed to replace conventional cuboid structure. Its resonance can be readily adjusted by modifying the substrate shape and the radiator size. The antenna operates at 2.54 GHz with fractional bandwidth of 3.51%, achieving a peak gain of 5.2 dBi at 2.54 GHz. Using the proposed method, the antenna achieves an area reduction of 41.74% compared to a conventional patch antenna.

articleTitle: A Wideband Circularly Polarized Magneto-Electric Dipole Antenna Array With Sequential Rotated Feeding For Wireless and Satellite Communication
abstract: A wideband circularly polarized (CP) magneto-electric (ME) dipole antenna array with a sequential rotated feeding (SRF) network for wireless and satellite communication is proposed in this paper. By sequentially rotating the sub-array and integrating with the SRF network, the impedance and axial ratio (AR) bandwidth are enhanced. The simulation overlapped bandwidth (|S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>|<-10 dB, AR<3dB) of the 4×4 antenna array is 57.4% (24.14-43.57 GHz) with a peak realized gain of 17.2 dBic. With excellent performance of wideband and stable realized gain, the proposed CP antenna array is a suitable candidate for wireless and satellite communication.

articleTitle: Dielectric Temporal Dynamics and Challenges Towards Accurate Skin Lesion Detection
abstract: This paper presents the current challenges of expanding our handheld skin cancer detection system towards large-scale application on different skin regions across the human body. The analysis is based on temporal dielectric trend assessment of common moles and adjacent skin regions. The study indicates that developing a robust skin cancer detection system requires consideration of additional factors, such as hair strand interference compensation and dermal hydration levels in parallel with dielectric data acquisition. These biomechanical descriptor variations, including trans-epidermal water loss, contribute to fluctuations in the dielectric properties of the same skin region measured at different times.

articleTitle: Frequency Tuning Range Enhancement of a Filtering Patch Antenna
abstract: A recently proposed low-profile frequency-reconfigurable filtering patch antenna is further optimized to achieve a wider frequency tuning range. The design realizes the filtering functionality using four parasitic strips and two lateral stubs. To achieve frequency-reconfigurability, sets of varactor diodes are integrated on the main patch, parasitic strips, and lateral stubs to vary their electrical length. The extension proposed here for the original design integrates thin copper extension lines with the varactor diodes. These lines bridge the parasitic strips, lateral stubs, and the main patch with their respective tuning elements, which reduces the parasitic parallel capacitance to the varactor diodes. As a result, the proposed evolved design shows a 31.5% frequency tuning range, which is 9.6% wider compared to the original design.

articleTitle: A Microwave Twin-Port Probe for Non-Invasive Skin Cancer Detection
abstract: This paper presents a novel microwave twin-port coaxial probe integrated with a coplanar waveguide (CPW) transmission line for non-invasive skin cancer detection. Operating at approximately 14 GHz, the probe utilizes both reflection and transmission-based analyses. The design was evaluated through full-wave simulations, and the results demonstrate the probe’s capability to differentiate the dielectric properties of various materials.

articleTitle: Miniaturized 3-D Printable Composite Metasurface for 1-D Beam Steering
abstract: This paper presents a 3-D-printable metal-dielectric unit cell-based composite metasurface with a lower profile for 1-D beam steering of aperture-type antennas. The proposed metasurface also incorporates near-field phase correction to enhance far-field radiation performance. Two types of highly transmitting unit cells are introduced to achieve a wide range of transmission phase delays. The efficacy of the proposed metasurface is analyzed numerically in conjunction with a resonant cavity antenna. The system can steer the beam 360° in the azimuth plane (ϕ), with a predefined beam tilting in the elevation plane (θ). Moreover, the directivity deviation is minimal, at 1.53 dB, across the beam steering range, coupled with excellent impedance matching.

articleTitle: Rectangular Waveguide TE10 to Substrate Integrated Waveguide TE20 Probe-less Mode Converter for Planar Terahertz Applications
abstract: This paper presents a novel design of mode converter for planar terahertz (THz) applications, which converts the rectangular waveguide (RWG) TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf> mode to substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">20</inf> mode. Unlike other converters that use probes for impedance matching during the conversion, this converter utilizes the stepped width of SIW’s top metallic layer to match the impedance during the transition. A back-to-back converter is designed and simulated to cover the frequency range of 1.25 - 1.32 THz, showing a return loss of 15 dB and an average insertion loss of 1.28 dB for the whole bandwidth.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Frequency Reconfigurable Patch Antenna for Wireless Power Transfer
abstract: This paper introduces a miniaturized frequency-reconfigurable receiving antenna incorporating a tri-turn square-shaped complementary spiral resonator (3-SCSR) for Wireless Power Transfer (WPT). The proposed planar antenna features a simple design, with compact dimensions of 50 mm × 50 mm, and supports four operating modes. To achieve miniaturization, the 3-SCSR structure is embedded into the ground layer of the patch antenna. Three PIN diodes are integrated with the 3-SCSR structure on the underside, enabling reconfigurable operation across single, dual, and tri-band modes over a wide frequency range (0.205–1.7 GHz), achieving a peak antenna gain of 2.84 dBi. Additionally, a matching network and rectifier designed for 1.5 GHz enable RF-DC conversion, delivering 50% efficiency at an input power as low as –10 dBm.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Curved Cylindrical Waveguide Sensor for Early Detection of Melanoma
abstract: This paper explores using RFID sensing technology to monitor soft skin moisture, enhance skincare routines, and improve health management. The proposed sensor features a curved cylindrical Teflon or Rogers AD 600 core coated with copper film, with a segment removed to create a sensing section. An analysis of the sensor's electric field response and power flow on the skin reveals significant differences in transmitted wave values between dry skin and melanoma in the 76 GHz to 80 GHz range, enabling precise detection of skin moisture levels.

articleTitle: Frequency-Reconfigurable Ultra-wideband Phased Array with Enhanced Beam-scanning Performance
abstract: This paper reports a frequency-reconfigurable tightly-coupled dipole array (TCDA) with an overall combined 15.8:1 bandwidth and an enhanced beam-scanning performance. The scan volume expansion is achieved by incorporating a tailored WAIM design formed by dual-level, double-sided capacitively loaded loops (DSDL-CLLs). The DSDL-CLLs also facilitate the array achieving an improved impedance matching performance. Wide beam scanning up to ±70° in the E-/D-planes and ±50° in the H-plane with a VSWR < 3 is attained. The fabricated prototype of this innovative TDCA array confirmed its superior performance characteristics.

articleTitle: Continuously Tunable K/Ka-Band Phase Shifter Implemented Using Coplanar Waveguides
abstract: A continuously tunable phase shifter operating from 20 GHz to 30 GHz based on a broadside-coupled structure is presented. In this design, the broadside-coupled structure is constructed using a grounded coplanar waveguide instead of a microstrip line or stripline. As a result, the proposed structure can be implemented on both sides of a single piece of printed circuit board, leading to reduced manufacturing complexity and cost. To validate the proposed structure, a tunable phase shifter operating from 20 GHz to 30 GHz is designed and fabricated. The measured results show that the return loss of the design is above 10 dB across the entire operating bandwidth. Meanwhile, the design achieves a tunable phase shift range of more than 90° with ±6.7° phase imbalance and the insertion loss is below 1.25 dB from 20 GHz to 30 GHz. The simple structure and the achieved performance make the proposed design a promising candidate for building tunable feeding networks in the upcoming K/Ka-band low Earth orbit satellite communications systems.

articleTitle: A THz Time Domain Spectroscopy
abstract: Terahertz Time Domain Spectroscopy (THz-TDS) has become a critical platform in advancing THz detection and imaging science and technology. This article provides a detailed and step-by-step guideline for constructing a free-space THz-TDS system, coupled with a rigorous analysis of the fundamental principles underlying THz-TDS.

articleTitle: FPGA-based UWB Pulse Generator for IR-UWB Chipless RFID Reader
abstract: Ultra-wideband (UWB) technology has gained traction for applications demanding high bandwidth, precise target localisation, and low power consumption. This paper presents an FPGA-based UWB pulse generator tailored for an Impulse-radio (IR) UWB chipless RFID reader. Using a low-cost FPGA platform, the design generates a square wave signal with a pulse repetition frequency (PRF) of 1-50 MHz. This base signal undergoes pulse sharpening to produce picosecond-scale pulses, achieving the bandwidth exceeding 500 MHz necessary for UWB communication. Such a high-bandwidth signal ensures better range resolution, meeting the requirements of applications of UWB chipless RFID readers. By implementing pulse generation and PRF control on an FPGA, our system combines low cost, flexibility, and scalability, making it suitable for diverse UWB applications.
